questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Come to a stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm and hand point upward, they are signaling a right turn. If you are following this driver, adjust your driving to expect a right turn.

questions.question: Which of the following is a dangerous habit in work zones?

options.text: Tailgating another vehicle
Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Always watch for workers and equipment on the road.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you want to go. For a left turn on a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect your stopping ability. On slippery or poor roads, slow down to maintain control. Driving too fast on bad roads makes stopping dangerous.

questions.question: Fog reduces visibility of vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Drive cautiously and reduce your speed.
Not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to better see the road and objects.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead—they work better in fog by lighting up the road and nearby objects.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, steering is harder. Reduce your speed and carefully drive to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at 55 mph.
The highest safe speed in good conditions is 55 mph.
You must not drive slower than 55 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest safe speed in good conditions is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed limit for this road. You can drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: A yellow light warns that it will turn red soon. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Continue safely and clear the intersection.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue safely and clear the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through and exit the intersection as quickly and safely as possible.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe distance gives you time to react to problems without sudden braking, which could cause a crash with the car behind you.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: A dashed line means you can pass. A solid line means you cannot pass. When they appear together, only drivers on the dashed line side can pass. Drivers on the solid line side cannot.

questions.question: When you enter a street from a driveway, you should:

options.text: Drive slowly so other vehicles and pedestrians have time to move.
Honk your horn so other vehicles and pedestrians know you are coming.
Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians crossing. Stop before you cross the sidewalk. Not stopping is against the law.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, you should:

options.text: Look toward the center of the road.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay on course. Do not keep your bright lights on in response.

questions.question: A red light is showing, but a police officer directs you to go through the intersection. You should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer directing traffic always overrides traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: Which factor affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: Factors that affect alcohol absorption include a person's weight, biological sex, how much food is in their stomach, and how many drinks they have had. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: When you see an accident scene, you should:

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not arrived yet.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not stop at an accident scene unless you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Keep your attention on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Never drive to an accident, fire, or disaster just to look.

questions.question: A good driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules are guidelines, but no one should assume they have the right-of-way. Always consider the situation at each intersection. Yield your right-of-way if it can prevent a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop before entering the intersection.
Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic already in the intersection or on the road you are entering.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at an intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can proceed without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are yielding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If you and another vehicle arrive at an open intersection at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they should:

options.text: Drive normally. Their emotions will not affect their driving.
Drive faster because they are more aware of everything.
Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
Call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can distract you from driving. Your mind may focus on your feelings instead of the road. Always calm down and get focused before you start driving.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Use low beam headlights.
Use high beam headlights until you are 10 feet away from the car ahead.
Use high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Switch to low beam headlights when you are following another vehicle.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with extra caution.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet makes the road slippery. Safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that should be used with low beams.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by an adult.
Are safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use a proper seat to secure children in a vehicle.

questions.question: The traffic light is green, but the intersection ahead is blocked. You should:

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Do not enter the intersection if it is blocked, even if the light is green. If you enter and the light turns red, you will block cross traffic. This can result in a ticket.

questions.question: Drowsy drivers:

options.text: Should drink strong coffee to stay awake.
Can drive so poorly that they seem drunk.
Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
Are usually older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can drive so poorly that they seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive as badly as drunk drivers. Opening windows, loud radio, or coffee are not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not affected.
Alcohol damages your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol damages your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms your judgment. Good judgment helps you react safely to dangers on the road. Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your driving ability.

questions.question: You want to pass a motorcycle. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and doesn't take up much space.
Honk to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder so you can pass.
Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Give motorcycles a full lane when passing. Never share a lane with a motorcycle. Returning to your lane too soon can force the rider to swerve into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early so other drivers know your plan.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early so other drivers know your plan.
questions.explanation: Signal early before you pass so other drivers know what you are going to do.
